keyVerseText: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, If any man of you bring an offering unto the LORD, ye shall bring your offering of the cattle, even of the herd, and of the flock.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun קׇרְבָּן (qorbân) stems from the root קָרַב (qârab), which means 'to approach' or 'to bring near.' This etymology highlights that a קׇרְבָּן is fundamentally something brought near, specifically near to God, as an offering. Unlike the general English term 'offering,' the root sense emphasizes the act of drawing close or presenting oneself or something in proximity to the divine presence, underscoring intimacy and intentional approach in worship.
usageInScripture: The word קׇרְבָּן appears 82 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is consistently translated as 'offering' or 'oblation.' It encompasses a broad range of offerings including animal, vegetable, and even precious metals, as indicated by its use in Leviticus, Numbers, and Ezekiel. The top translations such as 'this was the offering,' 'His offering,' and 'an offering' reveal that קׇרְבָּן functions as a general term for all kinds of sacrificial presents brought near the altar, emphasizing its role as a central element in Israelite worship and covenant relationship with God.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding קׇרְבָּן as an offering that is brought near to God enriches our grasp of biblical worship and atonement. It points to the necessity of drawing close to God through a tangible expression of devotion, sacrifice, and obedience. In the Christian faith, this concept foreshadows Christ’s ultimate offering, who draws sinners near to God by His perfect sacrifice. Thus, the word reminds believers that true worship involves both approach and presentation to God, highlighting the relational and redemptive dimensions of sacrifice in Scripture.
keyVerseReflection: Leviticus 1:2 commands the Israelites to bring an offering (קׇרְבָּן) of cattle to the LORD, emphasizing the act of bringing something near to God as a form of worship. The use of קׇרְבָּן here stresses not just the gift itself but the intentional approach toward God through sacrifice. This verse sets the tone for the sacrificial system, teaching that offerings are a means by which the people draw near to God in obedience and reverence.
